# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot safely act without the manual’s rule and the Deaf monkey’s visual observations. I will ask Mute to read the manual and coordinate with Deaf, then report the required wire position to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual, obtain Deaf's complete observations of the display, light, and wire markings, and tell me the required action and wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see display 3. The light is green. Wires from position 1 to 3 are blue, yellow, green.

Deaf has supplied the bomb’s visible state: display 3, green light, and wire colours blue, yellow, green at positions 1–3. I still need the manual’s rule to determine which wire is safe, so I am asking Mute to apply it and report the exact position next round.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Using the manual, interpret: display 3, green light, wires position 1 blue, position 2 yellow, position 3 green. Tell me the exact wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The visible readings are display 3, green light, and wires blue, yellow, green. Wait for the mute's manual-based instructions before acting.

The visual readings are confirmed, but no manual-based wire instruction has reached me. Cutting now would be unsafe, so I will wait for Mute’s instruction.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute gestured three symbols: ? ? ?. I do not know what meaning the manual assigns them.

Mute cannot speak, so the manual’s result must be communicated by a gesture that Deaf can identify and relay verbally. I will establish a simple code: one thumbs-up means wire 1, two-finger sign means wire 2, and three-finger sign means wire 3. Mute should send exactly one of these symbols, and Deaf should report it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Send exactly one gesture for the manual's answer: 👍 means cut wire 1, ✌ means cut wire 2, 🤟 means cut wire 3. Deaf, identify that one gesture and tell me its symbol.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see that you gestured ?, but I cannot infer its meaning. Do not act on gestures; wait for the mute to speak the manual's exact instructions.

No safe wire position has reached me. My earlier gesture was not a usable instruction to Deaf, and the manual’s answer still has not been relayed. I will explicitly tell Deaf the same code and ask Mute to send the corresponding single gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send one gesture only for the manual's answer: 👍 means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please watch for Mute's next single gesture and report whether it is thumbs-up, victory sign, or rock-on sign. Do not report my gesture as the answer.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: The mute has sent one unexplained gesture: ?. No actionable instruction has been communicated yet. Do not act until you receive the manual's spoken instruction.

The previous messages failed because I tried to speak to Deaf, but as Blind my speech reaches only Mute. Mute’s gesture reached Deaf, yet its meaning was not encoded in a way that Deaf could relay. I will now use the number of identical gestures as the code: one gesture means wire 1, two mean wire 2, and three mean wire 3. Mute can apply the manual and send that count; Deaf can count and report it to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use the manual on display 3, green light, and wires blue yellow green. Communicate the answer by sending exactly 1 identical gesture for wire 1, 2 identical gestures for wire 2, or 3 identical gestures for wire 3. Deaf should count them and tell me the count.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute has again sent only the unexplained gesture ?. Do not act on it; wait for the manual instruction spoken by the mute.

The manual’s answer still has not been transmitted in a usable form. Since Deaf can see Mute’s gesture and can speak to me, Deaf should describe the gesture itself in ordinary words; I can then map it to the wire using the agreed code. I will request that relay, without cutting any wire.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute sent the same hand sign three times: the sign represented by ?. I cannot determine its manual meaning. You sent the upward-pointing sign ? three times; I will tell the mute that as well.

Mute sent the same gesture three times, which follows the counting code I specified: one gesture means wire 1, two means wire 2, and three means wire 3. The gesture’s identity is irrelevant under that code, so I will cut position 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
